objective: Retain a current-main keyed DEVELOPMENT/TEST Chrome extension from automatic push CI so the owned native harness can test the actual pushed source without a local build or Store release credential.

source_findings.ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs pnpm wxt build on main pushes, tags, and pull requests, but uploads no unpacked output. Hosted release is a separate workflow gated on a scoped Supabase PAT and is unchanged by this proposal.
source_findings.identity: wxt.config.ts includes the checked-in public development key when MATRX_CWS_BUILD is absent. That key must produce cihdmkcdjjckfhjpgoedmgfpoljebaml, already in src/config/identity.ts with https://cihdmkcdjjckfhjpgoedmgfpoljebaml.chromiumapp.org/; no new build channel or redirect allowlist entry is needed.
source_findings.runtime_config: src/config/env.ts requires WXT_SUPABASE_URL and WXT_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, and auth uses optional WXT_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID. Existing Hosted release secrets have these three public runtime values. CI currently also has committed public .env.production, but an explicit main-push step should fail closed if any intended runtime secret is missing or invalid.
source_findings.receipt: scripts/record-local-dev-build.mjs records local_dev_unpacked/not_published, manifest/package version and a hashReleaseTree SHA-256. It requires .output/chrome-mv3[-dev] and a test-results output file, embedding an absolute runner path. The native harness requires that exact local path and rehashes the tree. The CI receipt cannot be used verbatim after download.
source_findings.collision: The shared checkout may have an owned frozen artifact in .output/chrome-mv3 or .output/chrome-mv3-dev. Import must never replace either path. The proposed strict layout is test-results/ci-artifacts/<40-hex-source-sha>/<decimal-run-id>-<decimal-attempt>/chrome-mv3 for unpacked bytes, with ci-receipt.json, provenance.json and local-dev-receipt.json as siblings of chrome-mv3. The existing recorder must admit both that build path and its sibling local-dev receipt path. Exclusive creation and an existing target refusal preserve immutability. SEO guest runner supports SEO_GUEST_EXTENSION_DIR and SEO_GUEST_DEV_BUILD_RECEIPT.

proposed_change: Only on push to main after existing checks pass, validate the three existing public runtime config values without printing them. Require WXT_SUPABASE_URL exactly https://db.matrxserver.com, WXT_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY in the sb_publishable_ public format (reject sb_secret_, JWT service_role, and any other key format), and a nonempty public PKCE OAuth client ID. Do not provide SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, DB service-role/admin secrets, or release authority to this step. PRs, including forks, and tags retain their ordinary build/check path but cannot receive or publish this test artifact. After build, verify the effective bundled values by comparing fixed expected configuration against emitted assets without logging the key or client ID; refuse if the values are absent or divergent.

Run the existing WXT Chrome build with MATRX_CWS_BUILD unset, assert keyed manifest version and exact development extension ID, and invoke the canonical recordLocalDevBuild helper. Preserve its original CI receipt and immutable CI source identity (github.sha, workflow run ID/attempt, manifest version, tree SHA-256) in an explicit development-only provenance file with eligibleStore=false and publish_state=not_published. Upload only .output/chrome-mv3 unpacked files plus these two small receipts as an Actions artifact named for the commit and run attempt; include hidden files and fail if missing. The resulting GitHub run must conclude success before import; a cancelled superseded run cannot be represented as current.

Add a small local import verifier that downloads by the exact GitHub Actions artifact ID, obtains run and artifact metadata from the authenticated GitHub API, and verifies repository armanisadeghi/matrx-extend, CI workflow, push event, refs/heads/main, successful conclusion, head SHA, run ID/attempt, artifact ID/name and GitHub's artifact SHA-256 digest against the downloaded archive. Caller-supplied SHA/run identity is only a selector, never the trust source. Independently verify the preserved original CI receipt and provenance against the extracted manifest version/key/extension ID and hashReleaseTree of the downloaded tree. Refuse if metadata, archive, or tree differ.

Import into the exact run-qualified test-results/ci-artifacts layout described above, refusing any pre-existing destination or symlink; keep ci-receipt.json and provenance.json outside the hashed chrome-mv3 tree. Extend recordLocalDevBuild and requireLocalDevReceipt only for this strict directory plus its sibling local-dev-receipt.json, retaining the existing .output admission, exclusive receipt creation, manifest/package version check, and double tree hash. The original CI receipt stays byte-for-byte unchanged. The new local path receipt is only a path rebind after remote identity and byte integrity are established; a native result cites original GitHub run/artifact identity, source SHA and the unchanged tree hash.

To call an artifact current pushed source, fetch origin/main and compare its SHA with GitHub's attested head SHA. Separately record local HEAD and tracked dirty state at import and native-result time. If origin/main has advanced, or HEAD differs, or tracked files are dirty, label it only as an exact pushed commit artifact, never current working source; changed-source acceptance stays pending until those edits are pushed and their successful CI artifact is imported. Untracked files that affect a runner must be reported separately. Version equality alone never upgrades a source claim.

Use the imported path and its local receipt in native runners that accept both overrides. Where a runner hardcodes .output, update only when separately scoped; the first consumer is SEO guest. This development artifact never satisfies Store ZIP, published release receipt, release.sh, or upload gates.
validation_plan_after_review: Static syntax and focused helper tests for authenticated run/artifact/digest verification, exact SHA/version/hash/ID, dirty or advanced source labeling, collision/symlink refusal, credential-shape and emitted-config verification, and PR/tag exclusion; no local build or native launch in this lane.

After main push, inspect the exact successful CI run and GitHub artifact metadata, download by artifact ID, verify/import without clobbering frozen173, and hand the new native path/receipt to the root owner for resource-admitted SEO test. Source commit 94bfae67 includes the newly pushed SEO repair; only an artifact whose attested head SHA includes that commit can exercise it. Report the run/artifact ID, GitHub archive digest and imported tree hash; do not claim native pass until the owned browser run completes.
